desc: Derive the exact BFS-layer characterization: L0={1}; every vertex in layer i≥1 has at least one neighbor in layer i-1; edges only inside a layer or between adjacent layers; no edges between layers differing by ≥2.
Prove that summing over ordered layer-size compositions with labeled assignments counts each qualifying graph exactly once, with parity condition sum of even-indexed layer sizes = N/2.
Derive the edge generating function for fixed consecutive layer sizes a,b as ((1+x)^a - 1)^b for required cross edges times (1+x)^{C(b,2)} for inside the new layer.
Build a DP over used vertices n, even-layer count e, last layer size a, and next-layer parity, storing polynomials truncated to degree N(N-1)/2.
Implement binomial coefficients up to 435 modulo arbitrary prime P safely.
Fix the missing labeled choice factor in transitions: multiply by C(N-used, b) modulo P when adding a layer of size b.
Run the corrected program on the three provided samples and on the N=2 edge case, record outputs and runtime, and report any mismatch or timeout.
Add and run a brute-force verifier for N<=6 that enumerates all graphs, computes BFS parity from vertex 1, and compares all M coefficients against the DP.
If samples mismatch, debug layer parity handling, labeled assignment factors, terminal-state filtering, and truncation bounds.

If samples match but runtime is too high, implement tight degree bounds, cache transition polynomials/nonzero degrees, prune states that cannot reach even=N/2, and use sparse or compiled/vectorized convolution where beneficial.
Re-run full validation after optimizations and finalize the fastest correct Python version.
